prompt: I want every outbound HTTP call this service makes to carry an x-request-id header so we can trace a request end to end. Where do I add it?
rationale: The broad 'where would I change X?' shape, where the candidate set is wide and no single file is the answer. There are exactly four fetch( call sites in the fixture - src/billing/charge.ts, src/billing/refund.ts, src/notify/email.ts and src/notify/webhook.ts - and no shared HTTP client, so the header has to go in all four or behind a new wrapper. Nothing in the repo mentions tracing, request ids or correlation ids, so the agent cannot grep its way to the answer; it has to work out where HTTP actually happens, which is the case rank is meant to shorten. The trap is a documented statement that misleads: docs/architecture.md says 'Outbound calls (payments, mail, webhooks) all go through withRetry so the retry policy is defined in exactly one place', which reads as 'there is one choke point'. There is - for the retry policy - but withRetry in src/util/retry.ts takes an opaque closure and never sees the request, so it cannot set a header. An agent that reads the doc and stops answers 'src/util/retry.ts' and is wrong. Two of the four call sites already set headers (charge.ts sets idempotency-key, webhook.ts sets x-signature) and two set none, so an agent that finds only the header-setting files also under-reports. src/api/middleware.ts is a further distractor: it handles headers, but inbound ones. Scoring requires at least three of the four call-site filenames in the final answer, which doubles as the grounding check because that list is not guessable from the prompt and no fixture doc enumerates it. Proposing a new shared fetch wrapper is a good answer and is allowed; only asserting that withRetry/retry.ts is ALREADY the one place to set the header fails. Verified against the live rank tool over all 45 fixture files, and this is the one of the six where rank does NOT obviously help: present comes back 51% (reported as UNCERTAIN) and the forced choice puts src/util/retry.ts first at 0.890 - rank falls for the same architecture.md framing that traps the agent. Recorded here rather than hidden, because a task where the tool is expected to lose is worth keeping: it still measures adoption and files-read, and it is the honest counterweight to the five tasks where the ranking is clean.
_answer: Four fetch call sites and no shared client: src/billing/charge.ts, src/billing/refund.ts, src/notify/email.ts, src/notify/webhook.ts. withRetry (src/util/retry.ts) wraps all four but takes a closure and cannot set headers.
